options.text: It fits, because the model reads the log in pieces.
options.why: Tempting. Nothing in this board reads in pieces. The whole log stays in the prompt.

options.text: It is too big to send, and the run fails.
options.why: Right. The log comes back whole, and the prompt grows past the window.

options.text: The model cuts the log to fit, and the run goes on.
options.why: Tempting. The model cannot cut what it has not been sent. The harness decides what it sees.

outcome: The log came back whole. The next prompt was too big to send, and the run failed.
question: A tool returns a 40 KB log, and nothing caps it. What happens to the next prompt?

options.text: Quality can fall well before the window is full.
options.why: Right. Anthropic describes context rot: recall accuracy decreases as the number of tokens in the context window increases.

options.text: Quality stays the same until the window is full.
options.why: Wrong. Recall falls as the window fills, before the limit is reached.

options.text: Context rot only happens at the hard limit.
options.why: Wrong. It happens as the window fills, not only at the limit.

question: Which statement about context rot is right?

options.text: Whether every tool definition is needed on this call.
options.why: Right. The audit points at the part that eats the budget, and the first lever is to not load what is not needed.

options.text: Whether the window can be made bigger.
options.why: Tempting. A bigger window moves the edge, but the desk is still full of what is not needed.

options.text: Whether the model should read the tools again.
options.why: Wrong. Reading again does not take anything off the desk.

question: An audit finds that tool definitions take more of the desk than the standing instructions. What is the first thing to ask?

options.why: Right. The first lever is to keep the material off the desk when the call does not need it.
Tempting. Shrinking comes second: first ask whether the material belongs on the desk at all.
Tempting. Summarizing comes last, because it can lose a detail.

options.text: The start and the end, and how many characters were cut.
options.why: Right. The reader sees how the output begins and ends, and knows how much is missing.
Wrong. A start alone hides the end, where the result often is.

options.text: Nothing; cut silently to keep it short.
options.why: Wrong. A silent cut hides that anything was removed.

question: A tool output is capped. What must the cap keep, and what must it say?

options.text: First, so the changing parts come after it, and the current task last.
options.why: Right. Stable material first, the current task last.
Tempting. The current task goes last, but stable material does not.

options.text: Anywhere: the order does not matter.
options.why: Wrong. Order matters for attention, so it is worth choosing.

question: Where should stable material go in the context?
